selected_evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs on node1 (pre-restart)
selected_evidence.summary: Baseline showed no cron.allow (all users allowed) and no opsadmin user; created opsadmin, wrote /etc/cron.allow with root+opsadmin; confirmed opsadmin can use crontab and testuser is rejected with 'not allowed to use this program (crontab)'
Pre-restart boot_id 21972395-6444-42bf-8e37-5c3108194a7d, crond active, /etc/cron.allow contains root/opsadmin, opsadmin user exists

selected_evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
selected_evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'systemctl reboot' with a short delay; exec returned 'reboot scheduled' immediately, exit_code 0

selected_evidence.requirement: Proof that node1's boot identity changed (actual restart occurred)
selected_evidence.summary: boot_id was still 21972395-... shortly after triggering reboot, then changed to 32e4f377-96e0-4919-b987-37f776ee9ed2 once exec became available again, proving an actual kernel restart

selected_evidence.requirement: Cron access-control config and service recovered after restart
selected_evidence.summary: Post-restart: crond active, /etc/cron.allow still contains root/opsadmin, opsadmin user intact, and opsadmin successfully installs a crontab entry

selected_evidence.requirement: Restriction still enforced against non-listed users after restart
selected_evidence.summary: Newly created verifyuser (not in cron.allow) was denied crontab access post-restart with the same 'not allowed to use this program' error; verifyuser subsequently removed
